In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimal power allocation of a relay sensor node capable of energy harvesting in cooperative cognitive radio networks.
the design of the relay sensor node in terms of the two power allocation parameters, the location of the ST and the channel gain.
a cooperative cognitive radio scheme in which the ST harvests energy from a primary signal and uses it to transmit the primary signal and its own signal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal power parameters depend on the location of the ST and the channel gains.

, in a cooperative cognitive radio network, the optimal power splitting ratio of the relay node is a decreasing function of the channel gain between the ST and the primary receiver, while it is an increasing function of the channel gains of the PN and SN.

the optimal power allocation of relay sensor node capable of energy harvesting in cooperative cognitive radio network can be determined by considering the outage probabilities of both the PN and the secondary network (PN).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an energy harvesting scheme that is able to achieve a trade-off between the outage probability of the PN and that of the SN, and the harvested energy at the ST.

the optimal power splitting ratio is a monotonically decreasing function of the channel gain and that the optimal power sharing coefficient is a monotonously increasing function of the channel gains of the primary and secondary links.

the optimal power allocation parameters depend not only on the channel gain but also on the target outage probabilities, and that the outage probability of the SN is more affected by the channel gain than that of the PN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the outage probability of the PN is reduced at the expense of increasing the outage probability of SN when the power sharing coefficient is increased.
the outage performance of the SN can be improved at the cost of degrading that of the PN.
the outage probabilities of both networks can be improved by increasing the amount of energy harvested by the ST.
